gap: No result ChatGPT got states the cost per added 1920×1200 screen at the maker's store today: $166.66 per screen for the FOPO S788 ($499.99 ÷ 3) and $200.00 per screen for the FOPO S11 ($399.99 ÷ 2). The three-screen S788 adds 50% more pixels than the two-screen S11 for $100 more.
standout_why: I compared against the UPERFECT '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders in 2026' page, which ChatGPT cited, and the WorkCocoon '16-inch extenders' page. UPERFECT lists a price, screen count and weight for each model, including the FOPO S9G at $299.99, 2 × 16-inch 1920 × 1200 and 2.4 kg. That means a reader can work out cost per screen from it, but the page never states it, and it doesn't cover the S11 or S788. WorkCocoon gives no prices, weights or power figures. ChatGPT's own answers gave the S11 at $399.99 and the S788 at 'about $500' but never put them on a per-screen or per-pixel basis. I couldn't open the FOPO and VueXtend product pages (HTTP 429) or the Best Buy INVZI page (timeout).
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. For a true three-display setup (laptop plus two 1920×1200 panels), the FOPO S11 at $200.00 per added screen costs the same as ChatGPT's INVZI pick at its quoted $399. I couldn't open a page to confirm the INVZI price, though. The S788 is cheaper per screen and per pixel, but it makes a four-display setup and needs the UsbDisplay driver, so it only wins if the shopper wants a fourth screen. The S9G is cheapest at $150 per screen, but that price comes from UPERFECT's blog, not FOPO's store.
